answer: Each new agent identity must solve a memory-hard Argon2 puzzle keyed to its public key and the current epoch seed, then maintain a continuous stream of micro-attestations drawn from a rotating lagoon of random peers. Three missed epochs drop weight to the nadir. A farm of 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 separate high-RAM processes and 1,000 distinct attestation schedules; the honest meadow pays the cost once. Attacker expenditure therefore scales linearly with identity count while extractable reward does not.
